key_insight: SAGE-PINN embeds axisymmetric cylindrical geometry and conservation laws directly into a PINN to remove the axis singularity and learn multiphysics flow without labeled data.
engineering_relevance: This enables mesh-free surrogate modeling for stenosed-artery-like axisymmetric flows and heat transfer, with stable physics-consistent predictions across changing buoyancy and advection regimes.
method: Use parity-preserving variable s = r^2 and a modified stream-function to eliminate explicit 1/r singular terms.
Enforce boundary conditions exactly with analytical, boundary-fitted ansätze.
Stabilize training with staged momentum-thermal-joint optimization, residual normalization, continuation in Péclet/Richardson numbers, and a physics-scaled drift guard.
evidence_signal: Validated against finite-element reference solutions for steady nanofluid flow and heat transfer, achieving single-precision mass conservation and central-range errors of 1.6% in axial velocity and 9.1% in temperature.
watch_item: Accuracy degrades in the most difficult regimes: strongly buoyancy-driven slow flow and highly advection-dominated heat transfer.
paper_title: SAGE-PINN: A Singularity-free Axisymmetric Geometry-Encoded Physics-Informed Neural Network for Axisymmetric Multiphysics Flow in Cylindrical Coordinates
